subject: Urgent: NovaBay inference surge — latency, 5xxs and reserved-QPS shortfall
messages:
From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@novabay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Novabay SRE <sre@novabay.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency & 5xx spike impacting production (urgent)

Karthik —

We started seeing a sustained latency increase and a spike in 5xx errors on our dedicated reservation this morning (around 08:45 PDT). Tail latency is up ~3x and a subset of requests are returning 502/503. This is affecting our realtime scoring pipeline and several downstream workers are timing out.

Attached are a small sample of error payloads and a quick traffic graph. Our SREs (cc'd) are tracing the requests, but we need Redwood's help — we are on a reserved capacity plan and cannot afford repeated degradation during peak windows.

Please advise immediate mitigation steps and whether you can open a priority bridge. If this is related to a noisy neighbor or pool saturation, we need a fallback plan (quantized model variant, temporary burst, or routing to hosted capacity).

Emily
Emily Tran
Head of Machine Learning Platform, NovaBay Financial
emily.tran@novabay.com

Attachments: novabay-error-samples.txt (text/plain), traffic-graph-peak-0613.png (image/png)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@novabay.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency & 5xx spike impacting production (urgent)

Emily — thanks for the heads up and the samples. I'm opening a high-priority incident and looping in runtime (Mina) and infra (Vivek) to triage. We'll also flag this to our account executive (Marissa) for exec visibility if we need cross-team authorization for burst capacity or credits.

Immediate plan:
- Mina to surface queue/backpressure and KV cache status and recommend immediate mitigations.
- Vivek to check GPU pool saturation, noisy-tenant signals, and routing fallbacks to hosted nodes.
- If required, we'll enable temporary routing to a compatible hosted variant and push a canary quantized model to reduce per-token cost while we stabilize.

Can you confirm the peak qps window (timezone) and whether you have any active heavy-batch jobs that might have started during that period?

I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes until we have a mitigation.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Emily Tran <emily.tran@novabay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency & 5xx spike impacting production (technical triage)

On Sat, Jun 13, 2026 at 10:05 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com> wrote:
> Emily — thanks for the heads up...

Quick triage notes (observed via runtime dashboards):
- Dedicated GPU pool for NovaBay (res-vcpu-22) shows sustained 98-100% utilization on one shard between 08:40-09:20 PDT. Other shards are nominal.
- KV cache pressure increased (hot prefix). Repeated long-context requests caused high memory churn and increased kernel execution time.
- Error signature: predominantly 502 gateway / upstream timeout during model forward pass at tail latencies > 700ms.

Immediate mitigation applied (now):
1) Throttled expensive prefix cache population for NovaBay to reduce KV churn (reduces tail latency but increases token-cost slightly).
2) Enabled temporary routing policy to spill 10% of traffic to hosted inference pool with a compatible model variant (quantized-8bit candidate). This should lower demand on the saturated shard.
3) We are rolling a short-lived canary of a quantized variant to the hosted pool (watching quality metrics).

Follow-ups:
- Vivek to validate that reservation throttling didn't trigger other reservations to bleed.
- If noisy-neighbor detected, we will isolate tenant and provision short-lived burst nodes to meet SLOs.

Attachments: diagnostic-log-snippet.txt (excerpt) — included for visibility.

I'll post another update in 30 minutes.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Runtime Reliability, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Emily Tran <emily.tran@novabay.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 14:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency & 5xx spike impacting production (exec visibility requested)

Adding exec context — we observed a transient reservation shortfall: NovaBay's reserved-QPS bucket reports a mismatch vs. actual sustained QPS during the peak window (approx +18% over provisioned sustained rate). The saturated shard coincided with a KV-cache-heavy pattern which pushed kernel latency into the 600-900ms tail.

Immediate asks for authorization (Marissa):
- Approve emergency burst to dedicated pool (+2 GPUs) for 4 hours to absorb peak while we rebalance (this requires cross-team capacity move and billing authorization).
- Approve a one-time routing allowance to hosted capacity beyond normal SLAs while we confirm whether model quantization meets quality gates (clear rollback plan included).

If we don't get authorization, our fallback remains: maintain the partial routing to hosted (10%) and continue throttling prefix population. That will reduce errors but not fully restore headroom for heavy windows.

We should also prepare a customer credit/commitment letter if NovaBay is materially impacted — recommend Marissa engage commercial.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@novabay.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency & 5xx spike impacting production (mitigation and next steps)

Emily — quick status update and next steps following the incident: 

What we did (summary):
- Identified saturation on one shard due to a KV-cache hot prefix pattern; applied a throttle on heavy prefix population and reduced KV churn.
- Spilled 10% of traffic to hosted quantized-8bit variant while monitoring quality — initial quality checks pass for the sampled prompts you shared.
- Provisioned a short-lived burst (+2 GPUs) in the dedicated pool for 3 hours (authorization granted by Marissa) which removed the tail 5xxs for the observed window.

Observed impact:
- Tail latency returned to within SLO for the majority of requests; 5xx rate dropped to baseline within the mitigation window.
- We continue to monitor for the next 48 hours and will provide token-level cost delta and a short RCA.

Recommended customer actions (for NovaBay):
1) If possible, stagger any heavy batch scoring jobs outside your realtime peak window for the next 48 hours while we stabilize routing and cache heat maps.
2) Share a short list of representative prompts that must keep 1.0 quality so we can run a deeper regression on the quantized model.

Commercial/exec notes:
- We will prepare an incident RCA and a proposal for a more durable reserved-QPS uplift or autoscaling policy for NovaBay's reservation to avoid repeated manual bursts.
- Marissa will follow up about a goodwill credit for the affected minutes.

Thanks for your patience — we'll keep the on-call watch active and circle back with the RCA and cost delta tomorrow.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Attachments: post-mitigation-telemetry.pdf (summary), incident-bridge-recording-link (drive)
